questions.text: GoatBank returns the allowCredentials list for every user name typed on the sign in page, and an empty list for unknown users. What is the risk?

solutions.1: None, credential IDs are public values
solutions.2: User enumeration: an attacker learns which accounts exist and use security keys
solutions.3: An attacker can derive the private key from the credential ID

questions.text: Why must the relying party compare the origin in clientDataJSON with its own origin?

solutions.1: To make CORS work for the WebAuthn API
solutions.2: So an assertion obtained by a look-alike (phishing) site is rejected by the real site
solutions.3: Because the origin is not covered by the authenticator signature

questions.text: A security key is the only factor for signing in (passwordless). Which flag must the server require in authenticatorData?
A security key that always increments its signature counter returns a counter lower than the stored value. What does this indicate?

solutions.1: The clock of the security key is out of sync
solutions.2: The credential may have been cloned
solutions.3: The user has registered the key twice

questions.text: Why should adding a new passkey or security key require recent re-authentication?

solutions.1: Otherwise an attacker with a hijacked session can register their own key and keep access
solutions.2: Because authenticators refuse to register while a session cookie exists
solutions.3: Because the WebAuthn API only works on freshly loaded pages
